title: Rahane Picks Bumrah-Led Five-Man Pace Attack for 2027 World Cup, Leaves Out Shami
excerpt: Rahane chose Bumrah, Arshdeep, Prasidh, Siraj and the uncapped-in-ODIs Mayank Yadav on Sony Sports — omitting World Cup record wicket-taker Mohammed Shami, Harshit Rana and Bhuvneshwar Kumar.
body:
• Former India captain Ajinkya Rahane picked Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, Mohammed Siraj and Mayank Yadav as his five pacers for the 2027 ODI World Cup, in a Sony Sports video posted Saturday, October 24.
  • Left out were Mohammed Shami — India's highest wicket-taker in ODI World Cup history and the leading wicket-taker at the 2023 World Cup — plus Harshit Rana and Bhuvneshwar Kumar.
  • Mayank Yadav is the surprise pick: he has played 11 T20Is but is yet to make his ODI debut, while Arshdeep has 30 wickets in 18 ODIs.
  • The 2027 World Cup is co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2 to November 21; India open against defending champions Australia on October 7.

Rahane names five, and the omissions do the talking

Ajinkya Rahane has picked his five fast bowlers for India's 2027 ODI World Cup squad — and the names he left out are as notable as the ones he chose. In a video posted by Sony Sports on Saturday, October 24, the former India batter went with Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, Mohammed Siraj and Mayank Yadav, according to CricketAddictor.

"Pehla Bumrah, no doubt. Second Arshdeep Singh, third Prasidh Krishna, fourth Mohammed Siraj, fifth Mayank Yadav."

— Ajinkya Rahane, former India captain

Bumrah was, predictably, the first name. Siraj and Prasidh were both involved in India's 2023 World Cup campaign — Prasidh as a replacement for the injured Hardik Pandya, though he did not play a match as Mohammed Shami came into the XI. Arshdeep, the left-arm option, has taken 30 wickets in 18 ODIs at an economy rate under six, and is already India's highest wicket-taker in T20Is with 148 wickets in 101 games.

Shami, Rana and Bhuvneshwar miss out

The biggest omission is Shami. He is India's highest wicket-taker in ODI World Cup history and finished as the leading wicket-taker at the 2023 tournament, but he last played for India at the ICC Champions Trophy in 2025 — a gap Rahane's list appears to treat as decisive for a tournament still a year away.

Harshit Rana also misses out, despite being one of head coach Gautam Gambhir's trusted bowlers since his Test debut at Perth in November 2024 and having represented India in all three formats since. Bhuvneshwar Kumar is the third major name excluded, as Sportskeeda noted: the senior seamer recently returned to India's T20I side after a gap of nearly four years, following strong IPL seasons, but Rahane did not include his former teammate.

Why Mayank Yadav is the bold call

Mayank Yadav has raw pace that few Indian bowlers can match, but his selection is a projection, not a record. He has played 11 T20Is and is yet to make his ODI debut, so Rahane is backing him to translate short-format impact into 10-over spells on South African pitches that reward bounce and carry — a year before the tournament, with fitness and ODI exposure still to be proved.

The logic of the five as a group is variety: Bumrah's accuracy and death bowling, Arshdeep's left-arm angle and new-ball swing, Siraj's seam and aggression, Prasidh's bounce, and Mayank's outright pace. What the group lacks is a second proven World Cup campaigner of Shami's type — the bowler who, in 2023, changed matches in the middle overs. If any of the five lose form or fitness, Shami's name is the one selectors will return to first, precisely because his tournament record is unmatched.

The tournament ahead

The 2027 ODI World Cup will be played across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2 to November 21, across 12 venues, with the final on November 21. India begin against defending champions Australia on October 7 — Sportskeeda places that opener at Newlands in Cape Town — and then face Pakistan on October 10 in Johannesburg, per CricketAddictor's schedule summary.

Rahane's list is an opinion, not a selection, but it frames the debate Indian fans — including the large diaspora following the team from the US, Canada, the UK and Australia — will have for the next year: back the emerging pace group Rahane trusts, or keep a place for the most prolific World Cup bowler India has produced. The answer will likely depend less on reputation than on who is fit and bowling 10 overs a match by next October.
